meta.description: Proks is a caching HTTP proxy in Go: TinyLFU eviction, Markov-chain prefetching, invalidation via RabbitMQ.
stars.label: stars on GitHub
footer.about: A caching HTTP proxy in Go. This site builds itself from the Proks README, docs/ and releases.
home.tagline: A caching HTTP proxy in Go that answers from memory in microseconds.
home.lead: It predicts which page will be requested next and fetches it ahead of time. It purges stale data on every replica at once. It knows nothing about your domain, so it fits any HTTP API.
home.stat_hit_note: HIT through the whole handler without the access log, Intel Core i7-10870H
home.stat_ratio_note: TinyLFU under a Zipf load, 50,000 keys, 1,000-entry cache
home.about_p1: Proks sits between clients and your API. Repeated GET requests are served from memory without touching the upstream. Responses with Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie or Cache-Control: private bypass the cache, so one user's private data never reaches another.
home.about_p2: Purge tags come from the route config or from upstream headers (Surrogate-Key, Cache-Tag).
mod.proxy: The HTTP handler: caching policy, collapsing identical misses with singleflight, stale-while-revalidate and refreshing hot entries before they expire.
mod.cache: Storage with TinyLFU admission: an LRU window and a count-min sketch. A one-off scan over thousands of pages does not evict hot keys: hit ratio 0.457 vs 0.260 for LRU.
mod.predictor: A Markov chain over route transitions plus an EWMA confidence score: decides which request is worth fetching ahead of time.
mod.prefetcher: A queue and a worker pool that fetch predicted routes in the background while the user reads the current page. p95 of the second request in a chain −22%.
mod.events: Invalidation across replicas via RabbitMQ: transactional outbox, at-least-once delivery, duplicates dropped by event_id.
mod.observability: Prometheus metrics: hits, misses, prefetches and upstream requests. Hit ratio and the benchmarks are computed from them.
docs.note: The documentation is written in Russian and is shown as it is in the repository.
bench.lead: A/B test of Markov-chain prefetching: the “book card → its authors” scenario (k6/prefetch-chain.js) with prefetching off and on.
bench.about: The benchmark runs in GitHub Actions weekly and on every release: a Docker setup with PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, 20 s warm-up, 1 minute per mode. GitHub runners are shared and noisy, so watch the trend rather than a single point. The key metric is p95 of the second request in the chain (authors).
